'''''Vaccinium elliottii''''' ('''Elliott's blueberry''') is a species of ''[[Vaccinium]]'' in the [[blueberry]] group (''Vaccinium'' sect. ''Cyanococcus''). It is native to the southeastern and south-central United States.

==Description==
''Vaccinium elliottii'' is a [[deciduous]] shrub {{convert|2-4|m|ft|abbr=on|frac=2}} tall, with small, simple ovoid-acute [[leaves]] {{convert|15|-|30|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}} long with a finely serrated margin. The [[flower]]s are pale pink, bell-shaped, {{Convert|6–8|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}} long, opening in the early spring before the new leaves appear.

The [[fruit]] is an edible [[Berry (botany)|berry]] 5–8 mm diameter. There are two variants one having tart shiny blue black berries and the other sweeter type having a whitish waxy bloom over the otherwise blue black berries; they ripen from late spring (in Florida) through summer (in Arkansas and Virginia). Chromosome count 2n=24.<ref name="FSUS 2023 o861">{{cite web | title=Vaccinium elliottii detail | website=FSUS | date=2023-06-29 | url=https://fsus.ncbg.unc.edu/show-taxon-detail.php?taxonid=4713 | access-date=2024-01-28}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is native to the southeastern and south-central United States,<!--Texas is not eastern--> from southeastern [[Virginia]] south to [[Florida]], and west to [[Arkansas]] and [[Texas]].

''V. elliottii'' has been observed in habitat types such as mixed hardwood forests, swampy woodlands, floodplains, and longleaf pine ridges.<ref>Florida State University Robert K. Godfrey Herbarium database. URL: <nowiki>http://herbarium.bio.fsu.edu</nowiki>. Last accessed: June 2023. Collectors: Loran C. Anderson, Tom Barnes, C. Chapman, James P. Gillespie, R. K. Godfrey, Gary R. Knight, R. Kral, H. Kurz, Sidney McDaniel, Richard S. Mitchell, and Camm Swift. States and counties: Florida: Calhoun, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Jackson, Lafayette, Leon, Levy, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Wakulla, Walton, Santa Rosa, and Washington.</ref>

==Uses==
''Vaccinium elliottii'' produces a particularly large yield of somewhat sour berries. It is popular for late-season fruit.
